- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent high), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline at 5% below peak for 3–7 days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 5%+ from recent peak), model often fails to recognize it; adjust downward by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1% lag correction to forecast for 1–3 days after sentiment shift.
